title: A SIGTERM in a gate does not name its sender
what: Every place relay itself sends SIGTERM or SIGKILL (hang bounds, the leftover sweep, test-token waits, gate stops) writes one line naming itself, the target process id and the reason to the gate log or a shared log the gate log points to, so the next "stopped by SIGTERM" line names its sender or proves it came from outside relay.
why: Owner, 30 Oct, answered "a" to: land the gate-lock fix and record the sender next time. The 29 Oct SIGTERM (exit 143) of tests/test_gate.py::test_f11_a_project_that_does_not_ignore_ci_can_run_the_gate_twice and tests/test_land.py::test_land_inert_take_reuses_gate in a quick gate was never traced; the gate log now records the signal but says "sender unknown" (lib/relay_gate.py:428, review F2 of a-gate-test-is-stopped-by-an-unknown-sigterm).
failing_case: Quick gate on 29 Oct: two tests red with 143 != 0 while each passes alone; the log does not say who sent the SIGTERM.
pass_cases: A test that stops a gate through each of relay's own senders finds that sender named in the log
A SIGTERM sent from outside relay is logged as not sent by relay

question: Where does the signal log (the record of which relay process sent a stop signal) live while tests run?
options: a. One log per gate run, in the run's own temporary folder, shared by every test of that run and passed down like the test token pool
b. The owner's ~/.relay/signals.log, as the branch does now
because: the project's Python rule: tests use a temporary folder and never touch the live ~/.relay; one log per run also answers F1 (a stop sent from one test is seen by the others in the same run). Owner can reverse.
